name: ActiveState
description: Who Vets AI's Code? Open source software runs the modern software stack. That was true before AI code generators showed up, and while coding has changed, the use of open source hasn't. What's changed is the pace and volume at which open source software enters your environment, and who, or what, is making the call to bring it in. The result is more open source software, arriving faster, with less opportunity for anyone to ask whether it should be trusted in the first place. So the question isn't whether your organization runs on open source software. It's whether anyone, human or AI, is vetting what comes in before it reaches your cluster. The ActiveState Curated Catalog is the answer by giving platform and security teams a single, governed source for open source software, built from source inside SLSA Level 3 infrastructure, with full provenance and remediation on contractual SLAs. When an AI coding tool requests a dependency, it resolves against the catalog instead of an unvetted public registry. Developers keep the workflow and the velocity they already have, and security teams get a governance layer that holds at the point of ingestion, before the dependency ever reaches a build. The result is a software supply chain your security team can actually account for, whether the code behind it was written by a person or generated by an agent. Learn more at http://www.activestate.com.
